title: The Fungal Fortune: How an IT Veteran Cultivated a Multi-Million Rupee Mushroom Empire
summary: After a 14-year career in the tech industry, BTech graduate Vikramdev Mohapatra pivoted dramatically, returning to his roots in Odisha to establish a highly successful commercial mushroom farm. His venture, Ganga Bhumi Mushrooms, now harvests up to 600 kg of produce daily, generating over Rs 10 lakh a month.
content:
In an era where the siren call of the tech industry often feels all-encompassing, Vikramdev Mohapatra's story serves as a potent reminder that true innovation, and formidable wealth, can sprout from the most unexpected places. After dedicating 14 years to the demanding world of Information Technology, honing skills in complex code and corporate strategy, Mohapatra made a decision that would undoubtedly stun many of his peers: he traded the silicon valley dream for the fertile soil of Nabarangpur, Odisha.

His departure from a stable, high-paying BTech-fueled career wasn't a retreat, but a strategic pivot into what he shrewdly identified as an untapped agricultural opportunity. Returning to his home district, Mohapatra didn't seek another cubicle; instead, he envisioned a verdant empire built on fungi. Thus, Ganga Bhumi Mushrooms was born, a testament to modern business acumen meeting ambitious agricultural entrepreneurship.

What began as a radical idea has blossomed into a formidable enterprise. Ganga Bhumi Mushrooms isn't just a hobby farm; it's a high-volume operation capable of producing a staggering 500 to 600 kilograms of fresh mushrooms every single day. This impressive scale isn't merely about production volume; it translates directly into a robust financial success story. Mohapatra's venture is reportedly raking in upwards of Rs 10 lakh a month, proving that disruptive ideas aren't confined to software or venture capital rounds.

Mohapatra's journey underscores a powerful narrative: the courage to redefine personal success, the intelligence to identify and capitalize on niche markets, and the tenacity to build a thriving business far removed from conventional career paths. His story is a compelling blueprint for how passion, paired with strategic planning, can cultivate extraordinary returns, even when the 'product' is something as humble, yet vital, as a mushroom. It's a testament to the diverse avenues through which true innovation flourishes.
keyTakeaways: Vikramdev Mohapatra, a BTech graduate, left a 14-year IT career to establish a commercial mushroom farming business in Odisha.
His venture, Ganga Bhumi Mushrooms, now boasts a daily production of 500-600 kg of fresh mushrooms.
The business generates an impressive revenue of over Rs 10 lakh per month, showcasing significant entrepreneurial success in agriculture.
author: Sanjay Sharma

title: Upper House Power Play: Rajya Sabha MPs Ascend to Key National Boards
summary: Ten Rajya Sabha members have been elected unopposed to various statutory bodies and parliamentary panels, including several AIIMS institutes nationwide. These strategic appointments see key figures like Ashok Kumar Mittal and Rajneesh Kumar Agrawal taking up significant governance roles in crucial national institutions.
content:
The halls of Parliament witnessed a crucial, albeit uncontested, redistribution of influence this week as ten members of the Rajya Sabha secured berths on various pivotal statutory bodies and parliamentary panels across India. These strategic appointments, made possible by the exact matching of candidates to available vacancies, underscore a quiet but significant shift in legislative oversight and institutional governance. It’s a testament to the intricate dance between policy-making and practical implementation, placing seasoned politicians directly within the mechanisms that shape national life.

Among the most notable selections are those to the prestigious All India Institutes of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) nationwide. Parliamentarians Ashok Kumar Mittal and Rajneesh Kumar Agrawal have been elected to the boards of these critical healthcare and research institutions. Their presence is expected to bring direct parliamentary insights and advocacy into the nation’s premier medical establishments, potentially influencing everything from resource allocation to strategic health policy directions. Beyond healthcare, other significant portfolios have been filled, with figures like Birendra Prasad Baishya and Sat Paul Sharma also securing positions on other vital statutory bodies, though specifics regarding their exact panels were not immediately detailed in the initial reports.

These appointments are more than just a matter of political procedure; they represent a deepening of parliamentary involvement in the day-to-day operations and strategic direction of key national assets. By seating its members on these boards, the Rajya Sabha enhances its direct oversight capabilities, ensuring a more integrated approach to governance. It also offers a direct channel for legislative priorities to be infused into the institutional frameworks, fostering greater accountability and synergy between policy formulation and its execution on the ground. This move ensures that the concerns and vision of the upper house can directly impact the functioning of institutions vital to public welfare and national development.

As these ten parliamentarians step into their new roles, the focus will undoubtedly shift to how their legislative experience translates into tangible improvements and strategic guidance within their respective bodies. Their influence, particularly within institutions like AIIMS, holds the potential to significantly shape India's future trajectory in critical sectors, demonstrating the enduring power and reach of parliamentary engagement beyond the legislative chamber itself.
keyTakeaways: Ten Rajya Sabha members were elected unopposed to key statutory bodies and parliamentary panels across India.
Notable appointments include Ashok Kumar Mittal and Rajneesh Kumar Agrawal to the boards of various AIIMS institutes.
These strategic placements enhance parliamentary oversight and allow for direct legislative influence on critical national institutions like healthcare and governance bodies.
author: PTI
